thread:
Ivy: Heads-up: DeutscheCare is negotiating a pilot. Requirements: EU-only jurisdiction (incl. CH/NO allowed), strict egress IPs whitelisted by their firewall, BYO-KMS in customer's account, and 30-day notice before any subprocessor changes. They also ask whether we can guarantee no analytics or metric sharing during the pilot. Can presales scope feasibility + cost? cc @Leo @Marta

Leo: Clarify scope: CH/NO included under their definition of 'EU jurisdiction' — we can treat those as allowed regions for routing (eu-west-1 + eu-central-1 + eu-north-1 + eu-south-1). Does customer require control-plane residency too?

Marta (acct): RFP: "Control plane and telemetry must not flow to non-EU/EEA/CH/NO subprocessors during pilot. BYO-KMS in customer's AWS account. Egress IPs must be stable for firewall allowlisting. Subprocessor-change notice: 30 days." They also asked for SOC2 addendum and DPA clause references.

Samir (ops): Feasibility check: Data plane can be pinned to EU regions listed. BYO-KMS in customer account supported via our HSM connector. Egress IP stability: we can provide a short-lived static egress NAT by peering into customer's VPC or by allocating dedicated NAT from our EU-only dedicated pool for the tenant for the pilot. Control plane: hosted control-plane lives in us; we'll need to offer mitigations for presales: disable telemetry, disable 3rd-party analytics, and route control-plane management via a temporary EU-only proxy to avoid non-EU subprocessors. Note: this is technical mitigation, not a contractual control-plane residency guarantee.

Ivy: Can we provide the 30-day subprocessor change notice during pilot? They require a commitment that we won't onboard new subprocessors that could touch telemetry.

Marta: Legal flag: we can't change enterprise-wide subprocessor policy for hosted offering. For the pilot we can commit operationally to freeze integrations for that tenant and provide a signed attestation of the freeze, but long-term contractual change requires Dedicated/Private.

Leo: Example pilot config I can propose to DeutscheCare:
```yaml
tenant: deutschecare-poc
regions_allowed: [eu-west-1, eu-central-1, eu-north-1, eu-south-1, eu-west-3]
control_plane_mitigation: eu_proxy: true
egress: method: vpc_peering_or_dedicated_nat
static_egress_ips: [54.38.12.45]
byo_kms: true
telemetry: disabled
analytics: disabled
subprocessor_change_notice_days: 30
failure_mode: reject
```

Samir: Ops steps: 1) confirm customer prefers VPC peering or dedicated NAT (peering preferred for security), 2) get customer's AWS account ID + CIDRs for peering, 3) test BYO-KMS connector with their KMS key ARN, 4) spin up temporary EU-resident control-plane proxy, 5) produce egress IP confirmation. ETA: 3 business days after we receive AWS details. One-time setup ops estimate ~$1.6k. Pilot ops overhead ~$900 for 30 days.

Marta: I'll prepare a limited attestation that states: "During the scoped 30-day pilot Redwood will: (a) pin customer compute to the customer's chosen EU/EEA/CH/NO regions, (b) configure BYO-KMS in customer AWS account, (c) disable telemetry and third-party analytics for the tenant, (d) use a temporary EU-resident proxy for management/control-plane signaling, and (e) freeze non-essential subprocessors for the duration of the pilot (no changes without 30 days' notice)." Will note attestation is time-limited and not a replacement for Dedicated/Private contractual commitments.

Ivy: They also asked about key rotation: can we support customer-initiated key rotation in their KMS during the pilot without downtime?

Samir: Yes, BYO-KMS supports rotation if they use multi-version keys and we fetch keys via our connector; we'll need to test it. Recommend they rotate once during staging to validate. We'll include rotation test in runbook.

ops-bot: Ticket INF-9933 created: "DeutscheCare EU-residency POC: static egress + BYO-KMS + subproc-freeze" assigned to Samir.

Leo: SE deliverable: 1-page runbook + CLI steps for peering & NAT + egress IP list + attestation draft. I'll upload artifacts in 6 hours.

Marta: Legal to confirm addendum language references and DPA clause snippets. I'll attach to attestation draft.

Ivy: Great — please keep thread updates. If they accept the attestation I'll get their AWS details and push on peering. :thumbsup:
